example.en: I am from America, and you are from Romania.
example.ro: Eu sunt din America, iar tu ești din România.

notes: The most irregular Romanian verb. Its present tense must simply be memorized — it does not follow any conjugation pattern.
Also irregular, and doubles as the auxiliary for perfectul compus (am, ai, a, am, ați, au + participle).

example.en: I would like a coffee, please.
example.ro: Aș vrea o cafea, vă rog.

notes: Note that ei vor ('they want') looks identical to the future auxiliary vor — context tells them apart.

example.en: Can you speak more slowly, please?
example.ro: Poți să vorbești mai încet, te rog?

notes: A modal verb, almost always followed by să + subjunctive: pot să merg ('I can go').

example.en: Yesterday I went to the store.

notes: The perfectul compus participle mers never changes for gender/number — unlike many other participles.

example.en: What are you doing on the weekend?

notes: Used in many set phrases: a face cumpărături (to shop), a face duș (to shower).

example.en: I have been learning Romanian for three months.
example.ro: Eu învăț limba română de trei luni.

notes: A regular -a verb — the most common and productive conjugation pattern in Romanian.
Note the vowel shift ă→e in tu/el/ei forms — common in -a verbs with a stem ă.

example.en: I live in a big city.

notes: An -i verb with the -esc- infix in eu/tu/el/ei forms — a very common pattern for -i verbs.

example.en: I work at an office downtown.
example.ro: Lucrez la un birou în centru.

notes: Takes -ez in eu/tu/ei forms, a common subtype of -a verbs (like a lucra, a studia).

example.en: I wake up at seven o'clock every day.
example.ro: Mă trezesc la ora șapte în fiecare zi.

notes: A reflexive verb: the reflexive pronoun (mă, te, se, ne, vă, se) always accompanies the verb and changes position in the imperative.
An irregular stem change (mânc- → mănânc-) appears in eu/tu/el/ei present forms only.

example.en: Come with us to the restaurant!

notes: The imperative vino! is irregular — it does not simply drop the ending like most -i verbs.

example.en: In the morning I drink a coffee with milk.
example.ro: Dimineața beau o cafea cu lapte.

notes: Short and irregular. Note that eu and ei share the form beau, and that the participle takes ă: băut.

example.en: I take the subway to the center.

notes: The stem switches between ia- and lu-: iau, iei, ia but luăm, luați. Used for transport (a lua autobuzul) and for ordering (Iau o cafea).

example.en: How much does a coffee cost here?

notes: In practice only the third-person forms are used, since things cost rather than people: Cât costă? / Cât costă acestea?

example.en: In the evening I read a book in bed.
example.ro: Seara citesc o carte în pat.

notes: An -i verb with the -esc- infix, following exactly the same pattern as a vorbi and a locui.
Stem alternates u→o: joc, joci, joacă but jucăm, jucați. Used for sports and games; for a musical instrument Romanian uses a cânta instead.
Covers both 'to phone someone' (te sun mâine) and 'to ring' of the phone itself (telefonul sună).

example.en: The working day starts at nine o'clock.

notes: The opposite is a termina. Both are followed by să + subjunctive when another verb follows: încep să lucrez.

example.en: Will you give me your phone number?
example.ro: Îmi dai numărul tău de telefon?

notes: Very short and irregular. The imperfect stem dăde- is unexpected. Takes a dative pronoun for the recipient: îmi dai, îi dau.

example.en: I know how to swim, but I don't know how to ski.
example.ro: Știu să înot, dar nu știu să schiez.

notes: Knowing a fact, or knowing HOW to do something (știu să înot). For knowing a person or place use a cunoaște instead — the split matters and English hides it.

example.en: I've known Maria for ten years.
example.ro: O cunosc pe Maria de zece ani.

notes: Pairs with a ști: cunosc pe cineva (a person), știu ceva (a fact). Note the stem alternation o→oa in the el/ea form.

Impersonal: the form NEVER changes for person. Who must do it is shown by the following să-clause — trebuie să merg, trebuie să mergem. The conditional ar trebui is the standard way to give advice ('you should').

example.en: The train leaves from platform three.
example.ro: Trenul pleacă de la peronul trei.

notes: Stem shift e→ea in the el/ea and ei/ele present forms. Opposite of a sosi (to arrive).

example.en: How do I get to the station from here?
example.ro: Cum ajung la gară de aici?

notes: Also means 'to be enough': Ajunge! = That's enough! Very common in travel talk: Cum ajung la…? (How do I get to…?)

example.en: I'm staying at the hotel for three nights.

notes: The participle rămas is irregular — not *rămânut. Used constantly in hotel and travel contexts: rămân trei nopți.

example.en: I'll wait for you at the entrance at six.
example.ro: Te aștept la intrare la ora șase.

notes: Takes a direct object with no preposition — aștept autobuzul, not *aștept pentru autobuz. With a person it needs pe and a doubling pronoun: o aștept pe Maria.

example.en: I don't understand. Could you repeat that, please?
example.ro: Nu înțeleg. Puteți să repetați, vă rog?

notes: Participle înțeles, not *înțelegut. The phrase Nu înțeleg is one of the most useful things a learner can say — as is Puteți să repetați, vă rog?
Takes a dative pronoun for the person told: îmi spui, îi spun. Used for reported speech with că: Mi-a spus că vine.

example.en: I found a very good flat.
example.ro: Am găsit un apartament foarte bun.

notes: Regular -i verb with the -esc- infix. Appears in the fixed greeting reply Bine te-am găsit!

example.ro: Ne vedem mâine la ora zece.

notes: One of the few -ea verbs. Note the participle văzut (z, not d). Ne vedem! is the everyday 'see you!'

example.en: What did you say? I didn't hear.

notes: Everyday synonym of a spune, and more common in speech. Participle zis is irregular.
Cred că… is the standard way to open an opinion — far more common than 'gândesc'.

example.en: Put the book on the table, please.
example.ro: Pune cartea pe masă, te rog.

notes: Note tu pui, not *puni. Participle pus.

en: to hold, to keep; to last
notes: Also means 'to last': bateria ține două zile. Note the double i in tu ții.

example.en: I'll leave the keys at reception.

notes: Lasă-mă! ('leave me alone') is extremely common. Distinct from a pleca (to depart).
Reflexive a se duce means 'to go': mă duc la magazin — very common in speech.
Same pattern as a duce. Note the direction: aduc = bring here, duc = take there.

example.en: I'll write you an email tomorrow.

notes: Participle scris. Takes a dative for the person written to: îți scriu.

example.ro: Magazinul se deschide la ora nouă.

notes: Opposite of a închide. Both have -s participles: deschis / închis.
Închis is also the adjective you read on shop doors.
Used for missing transport too: am pierdut trenul. Stem vowel changes to ia in the subjunctive.

example.en: I'm asking for the bill, please.

notes: Asking FOR something. To ask a question is a întreba — the split matters.
Pairs with a cere: întreb ceva (a question), cer ceva (an object or favor).

example.en: I'm going out for a coffee with Ana.
example.ro: Ies la o cafea cu Ana.

notes: Opposite of a intra. Also 'to go out' socially: ies cu prietenii.
Takes în: intru în casă. Note eu intru keeps the -u.
d softens to z in tu cazi. Participle căzut.

example.en: It seems like a good idea to me.
example.ro: Mi se pare o idee bună.

notes: Mi se pare că… ('it seems to me that') is one of the most useful opinion frames in Romanian.

example.en: I'll send you the link now.

notes: Participle trimis. Takes a dative for the recipient: îți trimit.
Regular -esc verb. Opposite of a trimite.
Plătesc cu cardul / în numerar. The noun is plata.
Note the vowel shift: eu vând but noi vindem. Opposite of a cumpăra.

example.en: I don't know what to choose.

notes: Participle ales, also used as an adjective ('chosen'). Subjunctive aleagă.

example.en: I try to study every day.
example.ro: Încerc să învăț în fiecare zi.

notes: Followed by să: încerc să înțeleg. Stem shift e→ea in the third person.

example.en: I managed to finish on time.
example.ro: Am reușit să termin la timp.

notes: Takes să: am reușit să termin. The noun is reușită (success).

example.en: I'll help you with the luggage.

notes: Takes a direct object with pe for people: te ajut, îl ajut pe Andrei.
Takes a dative: îți mulțumesc, vă mulțumesc. Literally 'I satisfy you'.
Source of te rog / vă rog. Vă rog să… is the politest way to make a request.

example.en: Can you explain it to me once more?
example.ro: Poți să-mi explici încă o dată?

notes: Takes a dative for the person: îmi explici?
Also means 'to look': Cum arată? = What does he/she/it look like?
Stronger than a plăcea. Te iubesc is reserved for real affection, not casual liking.

example.en: I would like a coffee, please.
example.ro: Aș dori o cafea, vă rog.

notes: More formal than a vrea. Aș dori… is the polite way to order or request.

example.en: I forgot my keys at home.

notes: Careful: the reflexive a se uita means 'to watch/look' — a completely different verb in use.
Same forms as a uita but with reflexive pronouns and a totally different meaning. Mă uit la televizor = I watch TV.

example.en: I listen to music on the train.

notes: Takes a direct object with no preposition: ascult muzică, not *ascult la muzică.
Hearing (passive) as opposed to a asculta (listening deliberately).

example.en: I sleep seven hours a night.

notes: Stem vowel o→oa in the third person singular: doarme.

example.ro: Mă simt mult mai bine azi.

notes: Reflexive a se simți is how you say how you feel: mă simt bine.

example.ro: Bunicii mei au trăit nouăzeci de ani.

notes: Being alive or living a certain way. For residing somewhere use a locui.
Stem vowel u→o/oa. Colloquially 'mor de foame' = I'm starving.
Participle râs, also the noun for 'laughter'. A râde de cineva = to laugh at someone.

example.en: The child has been crying for an hour.

notes: Reflexive a se plânge means 'to complain' — same verb, quite different meaning.

example.en: I've played the guitar for ten years.
example.ro: Cânt la chitară de zece ani.

notes: Used for instruments too: cânt la pian. Never a juca for music.

example.en: I've been driving for fifteen years.

notes: Both driving a car and leading an organization. Permis de conducere = driving license.
The noun călătorie is far more common than the verb in speech.

example.en: I'm coming back on Sunday evening.

notes: Reflexive. Mă întorc în cinci minute is what you say when stepping out.

example.en: I'm in a hurry, I'm late.

notes: Mă grăbesc = I'm in a hurry. Nu te grăbi! = Take your time!
Without the pronoun, a îmbrăca means dressing someone else.

example.en: I brush my teeth twice a day.
example.ro: Mă spăl pe dinți de două ori pe zi.

notes: Mă spăl pe mâini / pe dinți — Romanian uses pe for the body part.
Cum te simți? is the standard 'how do you feel?'

example.en: I use the app every day.

notes: Regular -esc verb. Folositor = useful.

example.en: I want to change the booking.

notes: Also for changing money or transport: schimb bani, schimb trenul.
Opposite of a începe. Termină! = Stop it! / Cut it out!
Reflexive a se opri = to come to a stop: autobuzul se oprește aici.

example.en: I've worn glasses since I was ten.
example.ro: Port ochelari de la zece ani.

notes: Used for clothes and for sizes: ce mărime porți?
Regular -esc verb. The noun is mâncare, not *gătire, in everyday use.
Takes -ez: studiez, studiezi, studiază. More formal than a învăța.

example.en: I'm working a lot at the moment.

notes: Emphasizes effort more than a lucra. The noun muncă is the everyday word for work.
More purposeful than a vorbi — you discuss a topic with someone.
Reflexive a se chema = to be named: mă cheamă Ana. Distinct from a suna (to phone).
Takes a dative for the recipient: îți ofer.
Restaurant and online shopping. Note d→z in tu comanzi.

example.en: A new block is being built here.
example.ro: Se construiește un bloc nou aici.

notes: Regular -esc verb: construiesc, construiești, construiește.

example.en: I need to fix the bike.

notes: Everyday word for fixing things. The noun is reparație.

example.en: I clean the kitchen on Saturdays.

notes: The noun curățenie ('cleaning, cleanliness') is more common: fac curățenie.
Takes a dative for the person: îți răspund. Răspuns is also the noun 'answer'.
Ce înseamnă…? is how you ask what a word means — the single most useful question for a learner.

example.en: The book comes out in October.

notes: Same family as a părea. Used for things coming into view and for publications coming out.
Dispari! on its own is a rude 'get lost'.

example.en: I grew up in the countryside.

notes: Both intransitive (children grow) and transitive (to raise children or animals).

example.en: I didn't catch the eight o'clock train.
example.ro: Nu am prins trenul de opt.

notes: Also 'to catch' a train and, colloquially, to understand: am prins ideea.

example.en: Someone is knocking at the door.

notes: Participle bătut, not *batut. Bate vântul = the wind is blowing.

example.en: I broke my arm last year.

notes: For things that tear or snap. A sparge is for things that shatter.
For glass, plates, windows — anything that shatters.

example.en: I deleted the message by mistake.

notes: Everyday word for deleting files as well as wiping surfaces.
Nu atinge! is the standard 'don't touch' — though the negative imperative is nu atinge, using the infinitive.
Takes a dative for the person promised: îți promit.

example.en: I can't afford a new car.

notes: Reflexive a-și permite = to afford: nu-mi permit.

example.en: I admit that I was wrong.

notes: Same pattern as a cunoaște. Covers both recognizing a face and admitting a fact.

example.en: Can you translate this into English?
example.ro: Poți să traduci asta în engleză?

notes: Shortened imperative tradu!, like du! and adu!. Din… în… for the language pair.

example.en: I'm suggesting something else to you.

notes: Built on a pune, and shares its irregular tu form: propui, not *propuni.
Built on a ține. Takes a dative: îmi aparține.
Depinde! on its own is the everyday 'it depends'. Takes de: depinde de tine.
Almost always met in the past: m-am născut în… is how you give your birthplace and year.

example.en: Raise your hand if you know.

notes: Reflexive a se ridica = to stand up, to get up.
A arunca la gunoi = to throw in the bin.

example.en: Will you cut the bread, please?

notes: Note the shortened stem in the singular: tai, not *tăi.

en: to go up, to get on

example.en: We're going up to the third floor.

notes: Used for boarding a vehicle: urc în tren. Opposite of a coborî.

en: to go down, to get off

example.en: I'm getting off at the next stop.

notes: The -î class: note the â in the noi and voi forms. Cobor la următoarea = I'm getting off at the next stop.
The -î verbs that take -ăsc-, parallel to the -esc- pattern in the -i class.
Same -î pattern as a coborî. Mă omori! is a common exaggeration, 'you're killing me'.

example.en: I swear to tell the truth.

notes: The verb of the citizenship oath. Îți jur = I swear to you.

example.en: I defend my point of view.

notes: In the oath: să apăr drepturile. Note apăr with ă — apar is a different verb (a apărea).

example.en: I respect the rules of the house.

notes: Also used for keeping to rules and schedules: respect programul.
Merită! on its own = it's worth it. Nu merită = it's not worth it.
Used for problems, paperwork and errands alike: rezolv eu.
Formal register. In speech people often say sunt de acord instead.
Takes să + subjunctive: refuz să cred.
Takes să + subjunctive for actions: evit să conduc noaptea.
Puteți să repetați? is the phrase to have ready when you miss something.
The eu form ends in -i, unusually for an -a verb: continui.
Both winning a game and earning money: câștig bine.
Note the ă→e shift in the tu form: numeri.

example.en: We're collecting money for a present.

notes: Reflexive a se aduna = to gather (of people).

example.en: Will you lend me five lei?

notes: One verb for both directions — the preposition tells you which: împrumut de la (borrow from), împrumut cuiva (lend to).

example.en: I'm filling in the form now.

notes: The -ez- pattern. The verb you need for any Romanian paperwork.
For machines and systems. A lucra and a munci are for people.
Third person only, and the verb agrees with the BODY PART, not the person: mă doare capul (sg.), mă dor picioarele (pl.).

example.en: I suffer from allergies in spring.

notes: Note sufăr with ă in the eu form. A suferi de = to suffer from (an illness).
Sharing a flat, splitting a bill, and division in arithmetic.

en: to start (a device); to set off
notes: For switching things on and for setting out on a journey. Opposite: a opri.

en: to be missing, to be absent
notes: Îmi lipsește = I miss (something/someone) — the thing missed is the subject, as with îmi place.

example.en: I spend too much on coffee.

notes: Only for money. Time is petrec: petrec timp cu familia.
Always reflexive, and takes la for the topic: mă gândesc la tine. Distinct from a crede (to believe, to hold an opinion).
Third person only — events happen, people do not. Ce s-a întâmplat? = What happened?
A very Romanian verb: mă descurc covers managing, coping and getting by. Descurcă-te! = sort it out yourself.
Mă bucur! = I'm glad. Mă bucur să te cunosc = pleased to meet you.

en: to get upset, to take offence

example.en: Excuse me, where is the station?
example.ro: Nu te supăra, unde e gara?

notes: Nu te supăra… is the standard polite opener for interrupting a stranger — literally 'don't be offended'.
For changing address. Moving an object is a muta without the pronoun.
Odihnește-te! = get some rest.
Takes cu for the spouse: mă căsătoresc cu Ana.
Takes pentru or de: mă pregătesc pentru examen.

Almost always used in the third person with a dative pronoun, and it agrees with the THING liked, not the person: îmi place cafeaua (sg.) but îmi plac cafelele (pl.). This is the single most common agreement error English speakers make in Romanian.

en: to be called, to be named
notes: Mă numesc… is the standard way to give your name, slightly more formal than mă cheamă. Also used for things: cum se numește asta?

en: to stay; to sit; to live (colloquial)

example.en: Hang on a second, I'm coming!

notes: Stai! also means 'wait!' or 'hang on!' in conversation. Stau în București is a common colloquial alternative to locuiesc.

example.en: I want to become a teacher.

notes: Built on a veni and follows it exactly, including the imperative devino!.
Takes the DATIVE reflexive pronouns (îmi, îți, își), not the accusative ones: îmi amintesc, mi-am amintit. Writing *mă amintesc is wrong. Takes de for the thing remembered: îmi amintesc de tine.
Extremely common in speech, often preferred to a merge: mă duc la magazin. Du-te! = go on, off you go.

en: to be located, to be situated

example.en: The museum is located in the center.

notes: The formal way to say where something is — signs and official texts prefer it to este. Non-reflexive a afla = to find out.

example.en: I hope we see each other soon.

notes: Takes să + subjunctive: sper să vii. Sper că da = I hope so.

en: to exist, there is / there are
notes: Există is the impersonal 'there is / there are' in more formal Romanian, where speech uses e or sunt.
Third person only. Cât durează? = how long does it take?
Also colloquially 'to dash off': fug la magazin.
Running as a sport. A fugi is running away from or dashing somewhere.

en: to go for a walk, to stroll
notes: Always reflexive. A plimbare is the noun: ies la plimbare.
Scuză-mă / scuzați-mă is the everyday 'excuse me' — accusative, not reflexive, in that form.
Iartă-mă! = forgive me. Note the diphthong in the third person: iartă.
A râde is to laugh; a zâmbi is to smile.
Nu contează = it doesn't matter, one of the most useful short replies in Romanian.

example.en: I'm afraid I've made a mistake.

notes: Takes de for the thing feared: mă tem de câini. In speech mi-e frică de… is more common.

example.en: The train arrives at three o'clock.

notes: More formal than a ajunge — you meet it on timetables and announcements.

example.en: I'm looking out of the window.

notes: More deliberate than a vedea. A se uita la is the everyday spoken equivalent.
Takes cu for the person: mă întâlnesc cu Ana. A cunoaște is meeting someone for the first time.

example.en: Say hello to your mother from me.
example.ro: Salut-o pe mama din partea mea.

notes: Salută-l din partea mea = say hello to him from me.
A striga pe cineva = to call someone by shouting.

en: to be silent, to shut up

example.en: He was silent the whole way.

notes: Taci! is blunt — 'be quiet' at best, 'shut up' at worst. Fă liniște is the polite version.
Takes la for aspirations: visez la o casă. Am visat că… for dreams while asleep.
Stem vowel u→o/oa, like a omorî. The noun zbor = flight.

example.en: I don't know how to swim.

notes: Note the diphthong in the third person: înoată.
For crossing a street: traversez strada. The -ez- pattern.
Takes cu: semeni cu tatăl tău. A homograph of a semăna 'to sow'.
Built on a zice. Interzis is the word on prohibition signs: fumatul interzis.
Both teaching a subject and handing something over. Note predau in the eu form.
The verb behind every greeting card: îți urez succes, vă urăm sărbători fericite.

example.en: The children are playing in the yard.

notes: Reflexive for playing games or messing about; non-reflexive a juca for sports and roles: joc fotbal.

en: to stand up, to get up

example.en: He stood up from the chair.

notes: Reflexive of a ridica. Ridică-te! = stand up.
Așază-te! or the politer luați loc! for inviting someone to sit.

en: to stop, to come to a halt

example.en: The train stops at every station.
example.ro: Trenul se oprește în fiecare gară.

notes: Reflexive of a opri, used for vehicles and for stopping oneself: autobuzul se oprește aici.
Same -esc- pattern as a locui — very common among -i verbs.
